hero.title: Social Stratification in Gupta Age
hero.description: An analytical overview of the evolving Varna system, the rise of the Kayasthas, and the degradation of the Shudra status during the classical Gupta period.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of social norms from the early Gupta consolidation to the late Gupta decline.

cards.details: Rise of Chandragupta I; continuation of traditional Varna structures with emphasis on Brahmanical orthodoxy.
Chandragupta II & Kumaragupta I; solidification of land grants (Agraharas) leading to the emergence of a proto-feudal social hierarchy.
Skandagupta onwards; increased proliferation of sub-castes and the decline of the mercantile class (Shrenis).

items.title: C.A.S.K
items.decryption: Caste (Varna rigidity increases), Agraharas (Brahman land grants), Shrenis (Merchant guilds decline), Kayasthas (Rise of the scribal class).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming the Gupta age was 'Golden' for everyone; in reality, the status of women and Shudras significantly declined.
Confusing 'Kayasthas' as a Varna; they were a professional group/caste that emerged as a distinct social entity during this time.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Social Pillars

  • Varna System rigidity
  • Rise of untouchability
  • Land Grant Economy

Key Social Changes

  • Integration of Tribes
  • Professional Scribes (Kayasthas)
  • Status of Women

Social Hierarchical Mindmap

  • Varna System
    • Brahmanas: Highest prestige, recipients of land grants (Agraharas).
    • Kshatriyas: Continued as warriors and rulers.
    • Vaishyas: Status declined due to loss of trade links.
    • Shudras: Improved legal rights (could hear Puranas, agriculture focus) but suffered social alienation.
  • Emerging Groups
    • Kayasthas: Emerged as a new professional caste of scribes/bureaucrats mentioned in Yajnvalkya Smriti.
    • Untouchability: Explicitly mentioned by Fa-Hien; Chandala status worsened.
Social AspectGupta Period Status
WomenReduced to household sphere; Pre-puberty marriage (Child marriage) introduction.
Guilds (Shrenis)Shifted from autonomous bodies to state-affiliated regulatory groups.
EconomyLand grants created a hierarchy of intermediaries.
